cohort: The study participants included women experiencing postpartum mood symptoms who either attended a peer-facilitated postpartum support group (n=45 for follow-up) or were part of a community comparison sample (n=152).
finding: Participant satisfaction with the peer-support program was high, and program attendees showed significant reductions in depression symptoms from pre- to post-intervention, although their post-participation depression scores were similar to those of a community comparison sample.
mod_finding: Among program attendees, pre-post analyses revealed a significant interaction for time x delivery method, indicating that changes in depression symptoms might be influenced by the mode of birth.
